name: trend state hold short
note: Sliced institutional selling persists through a confirmed downtrend state; buyers of the dip are on the wrong side of an unfinished parent order.

name: sharp 3bar pop downtrend
note: A fast 3-bar rally in a downtrend is mostly short-covering and momentum chasing; it carries no new information and fades once the forced buyers are done.

name: squeeze release down
note: Range buyers who bought the narrowing squeeze have tight stops; when the envelope expands downward their stops become forced selling.

name: demand bull with trend
note: Exhausted sellers at a demand pivot inside an uptrend are running out of inventory; late shorts must cover into the trend.

name: demand bear with trend
note: Buyers who step in at a supply pivot inside a downtrend are counter-trend and get squeezed out as the trend resumes.

name: boom short in downtrend
note: Dip buyers and range fadeurs are caught by a downward boom bar in a downtrend and have to sell stops below the range.

name: trend dip under fast average
note: Weak longs and short-term traders sell the dip below the fast average in an intact uptrend, while trend followers and dip buyers absorb that selling.

name: downtrend pullback rsi7
note: Counter-trend buyers in a downtrend have to exit into resistance; trend followers add short into the bounce and overwhelm them.

name: vol-expansion dip in uptrend
note: A volatility spike down inside an uptrend is forced deleveraging and stop-run flow; those sellers do not choose the price and liquidity providers get paid to take the other side.

name: established downtrend wpr pop
note: In a persistent downtrend, bounce buyers are early bottom-callers whose stops sit just below and feed the next leg down.

name: deep overbought below ema50
note: A fast rally that leaves price still under the medium trend is short-covering and stop-driven buying; once it ends there is no natural buyer left.

name: persistent capitulation in uptrend
note: Three bars pinned at the bottom of the range means forced sellers have been hitting bids with no relief; the supply is nearly spent and holders who did not sell are strong.

name: persistent squeeze in downtrend
note: Three bars pinned at the top of the range in a downtrend is forced short covering; when the shorts are all covered the buying disappears.

name: short rally in downtrend rsi14
note: Counter-trend dip buyers and short-covering push price up inside a downtrend. Trend holders sell into it, and the late buyers are stuck with losses they cannot exit without pushing price back down.

name: short sharp 3-bar pop in downtrend
note: A fast pop in a downtrend is typically a liquidity vacuum or short squeeze. Once the forced buyers are done, price falls back, and whoever bought the pop pays for it.

name: short upward spike in downtrend
note: An upward spike inside a downtrend is stop-triggered buying by shorts who got squeezed. That flow is one-off and forced, with no lasting demand behind it, so the spike unwinds.

name: short pullback in established downtrend
note: After ten bars of downtrend, a bounce to the top of the 7-bar range draws in dip buyers who are fighting the trend. Trapped longs sell into that strength.

name: short exit from overbought in downtrend
note: Buyers who pushed price to the top of its range in a downtrend are the weak hands. When price turns down, they sell to cut losses and the decline extends.

name: short volatility burst down in downtrend
note: Volatility expansion with price at the bottom of its range triggers stops and margin-driven liquidations of longs. They must sell into a falling market and cannot wait for a bounce.

name: bear pullback rally sell
note: Counter-trend buyers lift price above the fast average inside a downtrend. Their conviction is weak and trend-following supply sits overhead, so the bounce fades.

name: calm downtrend drift
note: A quiet downtrend has steady seller flow, for example from hedgers and fund rebalancing. Dip-buyers keep showing up early and get run over slowly, so price grinds lower.

name: below-vwap bounce sell
note: Buyers lifting price toward VWAP after a stretch below it are holding losing inventory. Institutions who need to sell benchmarked to VWAP unload into the bounce.

name: sustained dip in bull
note: Extended weakness in the range inside a rising market squeezes out weak longs through forced margin calls. Once they are gone, the longer-term holders face no more supply.

name: bear acceleration
note: When 10-bar momentum falls through -50bp, longs who held for a bounce hit their loss limits. Their forced selling accelerates the fall before new buyers can arrive.

name: bear rally rollover
note: In a downtrend, RSI turning down from the 60s marks the end of a short-covering bounce. The shorts who covered are done and the buyers left are late and underwater.

name: persistent bear weakness
note: Price pinned at the bottom of a 50-bar range in a downtrend means longs are underwater and trapped. Their margin calls and loss limits keep producing supply.

name: below ema50 rsi5 overbought
note: Retail bottom-pickers buy the first sharp bounce under the 50 average; they hold no edge and their stops feed trend sellers.

name: downtrend breakdown continue
note: Breakdowns in a downtrend trigger stop-loss orders from longs and sell-stop entries from trend followers, which forces sequential selling that cannot be avoided.

name: bear relief top hold
note: A sustained 4-bar hold near the top of a 30-bar range in a bear regime is a relief rally that buyers overpay for; hedgers reload shorts there.

name: weak-trend bounce short
note: Bounce buyers meet supply from holders underwater since the last leg down. Those holders sell at break-even and cannot wait for more.

name: panic drop long
note: A fast drop is mostly stop-outs and liquidations, not new information. Whoever sold at the low was forced to, and the price tends to recover.

name: spike-up reversal short
note: An upward spike against the trend is short covering and stop-runs. When the forced buyers are done, price falls back with the trend.

name: downtrend breakdown
note: A new 20-bar low under the 200 average triggers stops of dip buyers and range longs. Their forced selling pushes the price further down.

name: sharp drop in uptrend
note: A drop of 2% or more in 20 bars inside an uptrend is panic or forced liquidation. It is not a change in the underlying trend, and the sellers cannot keep selling.

name: persistent oversold in uptrend
note: Two bars of oversold RSI while the price holds above the 50 average shows sustained selling that fails to break support. The sellers run out and the trend buyers return.

name: dip above long vwap
note: The price holds above long-run average cost, so most holders are in profit. A dip to the bottom of the range is impatient selling, and holders in profit do not sell into it.

name: downtrend rally fade
note: In a downtrend, late buyers chase bounces into overhead supply. Trapped longs from higher up sell into strength, and the chasers have no exit once the bounce fails.

name: bear spike-up fade
note: A sudden upward spike against a falling trend is usually stop-running of shorts or a market order chasing thin depth. Once the forced buyers finish, price returns to where the flow was.

name: neural short not oversold
note: Shorting only when price is not already oversold avoids selling into exhausted sellers. The counterparty is late longs who still have room to lose.

name: demand zone soft rsi
note: A demand zone touched while RSI is below neutral means price arrives at resting buy orders after sellers have pressed. Sellers there are late and the resting bids are patient.

name: smc long after sweep
note: Structure long after price sweeps lower is buying after sell stops were triggered. The sellers were forced by stops and stop selling once the stops are filled.

name: S sharp rally in bear regime
note: Sharp rallies in a down regime are driven by short covering and FOMO buyers. Neither has fresh capital to keep buying, so the move mean-reverts.

name: S bearish signal below VWAP
note: Below VWAP, everyone who bought during the session is under water. They sell on any bounce toward break-even, and the bearish signal marks the turn.

name: S persistent below VWAP
note: Persistent trading below VWAP means the buyers are all holding losses. Institutions benchmarked to VWAP keep selling at that benchmark and buyers cannot get out without selling.

name: L RSI7 recovery in uptrend
note: Forced sellers after a flush finish selling. When the fast RSI turns up from 30, short-term shorts who sold the low have to cover into an uptrend.

name: L fast cross in uptrend
note: A fast cross up inside an uptrend marks the end of a pullback. Shorts who sold the dip against the primary trend are forced to cover, and trend followers add to their longs.

name: L squeeze release up
note: A narrow-range period stacks short stops just above the range. On a release upward the shorts are forced to buy, and their covering is the fuel.

name: L arbm long on dip
note: The signal triggers on a dip below the fast average, where the marginal seller is a scalper taking a small profit. Larger holders do not sell at that level, so the dip is absorbed.

name: downtrend pullback to fast average
note: In an established downtrend, buyers who bought the dip back to the fast average are under water. Hedgers and trend-following sellers use that level to add, so the pullback gets sold.

name: downtrend shallow rally
note: Buyers in a rally within a downtrend are bottom-pickers and short-covers. Trend allocators sell into strength, so these buyers get run over.

name: pinned at range top under trend
note: Three bars pinned at the top of the range while price is under the 100-bar average is a counter-trend push. Buyers are running out of steam and are exposed to the larger trend.

name: volatile spike high fade
note: A volatility spike at a fresh short-term high means short-squeeze or stop-driven buying, not fresh demand. When the forced buyers are done, price snaps back.

name: sharp 20-bar drop bounce
note: A fast decline of 1.5% or more over 20 bars is driven by liquidation and stop cascades, not information. Sellers who exit in the panic sell at the low and are absorbed by patient buyers.

name: sharp 20-bar spike fade
note: A fast rally of 1.5% or more is often short-covering and momentum chasing. Once the squeezed shorts are gone there is no natural buyer left, and the chasers are left holding.

name: fade up spike below trend
note: Upward spikes against the trend come from forced buyers (stopped-out shorts, market orders in thin books); after the forced flow ends there is no natural demand left to hold the price up.

name: sell-off cascade continuation
note: Longs underwater below VWAP in an expanding-volatility decline face margin and stop pressure; they must sell into a falling market and that supply persists over several bars.

name: overextended uptrend fade
note: Late momentum chasers buying after a fast run are the marginal buyers; once the initial holders take profit there is no fresh demand and the chasers become forced sellers.

name: short 20-bar breakdown in downtrend
note: Longs with stops resting under the recent low are forced sellers when it breaks. Their market-order exits push price further down, and they cannot wait because their stops trigger automatically.

name: fade rally below trend
note: Short covering creates a quick rally against the main trend. Once the covering ends there are no natural buyers left, so price slides back.

name: S pullback to fast EMA in downtrend
note: Counter-trend buyers step in at the fast average and are the losers. Trend followers reload shorts at the average, and the buyers' stops sit just above it and feed the drop.

name: quiet grind down
note: A slow low-volatility bleed lets longs believe nothing is wrong, so they do not cut. Stops cluster below and get hit sequentially as the drift continues.
